title: The normalized completed-to-finite quotient proper scalar mate
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, schemes X and Y, a morphism f:X→Y and n≥0. Let a be a compatible coefficient change from the completed integral coefficient sheaves to the finite coefficient sheaves of exponent n+1, whose component at every scheme is the canonical completed quotient projection. For every object K of the unbounded derived category of completed integral module sheaves on X, the actual proper scalar mate finiteProperComparison(a,f) at K is invertible. No geometric finiteness, constructibility or Tor hypothesis is required. Here finiteProperComparison is only the mate definition owned by [lem-pur-compact-support-finite-proper-comparison-iso], and not the disputed generic invertibility theorem. Coefficient data are [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data] and scalar extension is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

source.place: Finite quotient compatibility of the proper/open realization; Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 6.7.7 and 6.1.13; Stacks Tag 0GL6. Reuse of the complete private quotient_proper_mate argument from QcqsCompactSupportFiniteMates, factored below the parent to avoid an import cycle.

proof.text: Identify completed and finite inverse-image ring identifications with the normalized coefficient identifications of SfCompleteDirectImageReduction. The underived restriction comparison is identity on sections, hence is its normalized comparison.

On K-injective complexes cancel the finite derived direct-image computation unit and restriction computation isomorphism. Both derived comparisons obey the same cochain-unit equation, so derived natural-transformation extensionality identifies them.

Transport the proved sf_projection_formula through the left-adjoint uniqueness squares for the two scalar extension adjunctions. Substitute the prescribed quotient maps, inverse-image ring identifications and proof-irrelevant coefficient-square witnesses. This yields invertibility of the actual quotient proper mate on any unbounded input.

proof_origin.note: Reuse and generalization of the already proved private quotient-mate argument; only the proper factor, with its actual quotient maps. The new module imports no consumer of the parent comparison.

theorem completedQuotientProperMate
    (a : Change (completed l E) (finite l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n)))
    (hmap : ∀ W, a.map W = projection l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n) W)
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X)) :
    IsIso ((finiteProperComparison a f).app K)
